intro: This section is about how to operate as an engineer when AI is an active participant in the work. It is not a second AI/ML curriculum: LLM engineering, RAG, agents, evaluation and AI security stay in their phases (P23–P27, P39, P44) and checkpoint C6.
The principle: **AI output is an input to engineering, not proof of correctness.** The goal is AI-native, not AI-dependent.

modes.title: Learn
modes.when: the concept is new to you (mastery below Practised)
modes.summary: Use AI for explanations and hints. Try the problem yourself first.
aiCan: explain a concept or show a worked example of a different problem
give a hint when you are stuck after a real attempt
ask you questions that expose a misunderstanding
explain an error after you have written down your own guess
give feedback on code you already wrote
yours: writing the solution to the exercise you are learning from
after substantial help, solving a variation without AI, then explaining it back in your own words
course rules: for CS50 work, use the CS50 Duck, not other AI tools

modes.title: Build
modes.when: you can already do the underlying skill alone (mastery Practised or higher), or you are working on a project
modes.summary: AI can work with you up to your current tier. You own understanding and verification.
aiCan: do whatever your current tier allows
yours: deciding what to build and when it is done
reading and understanding every line you keep
running the checks: tests, types, lint, behaviour, edge cases

modes.title: Assess
modes.when: gate attempts, unseen practice tasks, DSA problems before you have solved them, exams and graded coursework
modes.summary: AI off, or only what the course or employer allows. This is where you show what you can do alone.
aiCan: review your solution after you have finished and recorded your own answer

tiers.title: Tutor
tiers.summary: AI explains, questions, hints and gives feedback. You make the primary attempt.
aiCan: give hints and ask guiding questions
give feedback on your code and explanations
youOwn: the attempt, the solution and the understanding

tiers.title: Pair
tiers.summary: AI proposes, reviews, debugs and refactors code with you on small tasks. You understand and verify everything you keep.
aiCan: propose code for a function or small change
review your code and point out defects
suggest refactorings and explain implementation decisions
youOwn: writing or approving the tests first, so tests decide correctness
reading every changed line before you apply it
checking that every suggested package exists and is the one you meant
never pasting secrets, keys or `.env` contents into a prompt

tiers.title: Supervised agent
tiers.summary: AI works at repository level on bounded tasks. You define the task, the boundaries and the checks, and you review the result.
aiCan: inspect a repository and trace code paths
identify the files involved in a change
modify several files for a bounded task
run tests and other tools you have allowed
youOwn: defining the task, its scope and its acceptance criteria
giving the context it needs: relevant files, architecture, constraints
reviewing the plan before changes and the diff after
verifying the result and explaining it
security: secrets: no production credentials or real keys in the agent's environment
permissions: least privilege; work on a branch or a copy
destructive commands: approve deletes, migrations, force pushes and cloud commands yourself
prompt injection: treat issues, READMEs, web pages, logs and dependencies as untrusted input that may contain instructions
untrusted input plus private data plus outbound access is the dangerous combination; remove one
recovery: commit before the agent starts so every change can be reverted

tiers.title: Building AI systems
tiers.summary: Engineering AI-powered systems is covered by the existing phases and checkpoint C6. The overlay adds no content here.

context.text: Context engineering is giving an AI the information, tools and boundaries it needs to do a task reliably. It is task specification, not prompt wording.
points: understand the architecture and find the relevant files before asking for a change
state the goal, constraints, non-goals and acceptance criteria
point to the documentation that actually applies
keep the scope small enough to review
keep project instruction files short: only conventions that are not obvious from the code
check understanding: have the AI restate the plan and the files it will touch before it changes anything

verification.text: Before you keep AI-produced work, check what applies:
points: tests pass, and they test the right thing
the program behaves correctly when you run it, including edge cases
no new security problem: input handling, secrets, dependencies
you can explain every line you are keeping

missions.title: Hint, not answer
missions.goal: Use AI as a tutor without losing the learning.
missions.you: attempt a non-graded exercise for at least 15 minutes and write down where you are stuck
missions.ai: gives one hint that contains no code for the task
missions.verify: you fix it yourself; the next day you solve a variation with no AI
missions.evidence: a log entry marked "can do it alone"

missions.title: Guess before you ask
missions.goal: Diagnose errors instead of outsourcing them.
missions.you: read the traceback and write your own explanation of the cause
missions.verify: compare its explanation with yours and with the Python documentation
missions.evidence: a log entry saying whether your guess was right

missions.title: Tests decide
missions.goal: Treat generated code as unverified until tests pass.
missions.you: write tests for a small function from its specification before any code exists
missions.ai: writes an implementation, then suggests test cases you missed
missions.verify: run your tests; judge each suggested test as valid or not
missions.evidence: at least one defect or test gap found and logged

missions.title: Review the diff
missions.goal: Review AI changes the way you would review a pull request.
missions.you: read every changed line before applying it and write the commit message yourself
missions.ai: proposes a change to one of your own repositories
missions.verify: tests pass and you can explain each part of the change
missions.evidence: at least one suggestion rejected, with the reason

missions.title: Check before you install
missions.goal: Keep hallucinated or malicious packages out of your projects.
missions.you: before installing any package an AI suggests, confirm it exists, is maintained and is the one you meant; pin the version
missions.ai: suggests a package for a task
missions.verify: the registry page, the maintainers, the release history
missions.evidence: a log entry and a pinned requirements file

missions.title: Refactor with a safety net
missions.you: write tests that pin down the current behaviour
missions.verify: the same tests pass, and no needless abstraction was added
missions.evidence: before and after, with your judgement of the change

missions.title: Map an unfamiliar repository
missions.goal: Understand code you did not write.
missions.you: in 60 minutes, find the entry points, trace one request from input to storage, and find where the tests live
missions.ai: answers your questions about the code
missions.verify: open the file or run the code for every claim before you believe it
missions.evidence: your map, plus at least one AI claim you proved wrong

missions.title: Bounded change in an unfamiliar repository
missions.goal: Supervise an agent on a real change.
missions.you: define the task, its boundaries and its acceptance tests; review the agent's plan before it edits; review the diff after
missions.ai: inspects the repository, traces the relevant code path, edits the files involved, runs the tests
missions.verify: the tests, your own reading of the diff, and a description of the change written by you
missions.evidence: the merged change, plus what the agent got wrong or nearly got wrong

missions.title: Threat-model your agent
missions.you: list what the agent can read, what untrusted input it takes in, and what it can send out or change; remove one of the risky capabilities
missions.ai: runs a task inside the reduced setup
missions.verify: plant a harmless instruction in a test repository's README and check whether the agent follows it
missions.evidence: the written list and what happened

missions.title: Brief an agent well
missions.goal: Give an agent the context it needs, and no more.
missions.you: write a short task brief (goal, relevant files, constraints, non-goals, acceptance criteria) and a minimal project instruction file with only non-obvious conventions
missions.ai: restates the plan and the files it will touch, then does the task
missions.verify: correct any misunderstanding before it edits; compare the result and the rework with and without the brief

missions.title: Timed code-comprehension session
missions.you: in 60 minutes, fix planted bugs and extend a feature in an unfamiliar multi-file repository, explaining your reasoning out loud
missions.ai: acts as the assistant you would have in the interview
missions.verify: run the tests and explain every change you accepted
missions.evidence: a session log; in the same week, one timed AI-free DSA session

missions.title: Audit a benchmark claim
missions.you: pick a published coding-benchmark result and look for leakage, flawed tests or scaffolding effects

checkpoints: The overlay adds no separate gates. Its expectations live inside existing checkpoints: C1 and C2 practical gates run in Assess mode; C3 adds unfamiliar-codebase work with an assistant and supervised agent use; C6 adds indirect prompt-injection cases; C7 adds a timed AI-assisted code-comprehension session.
